item.description: - Dictating into the middle of a sentence now fits in: Rhino lowercases the first word (names, "I" and acronyms keep their capitals), skips the period the speech engine adds, and fixes the spacing at the join. Short dictations of one to three words at the start of a field or line, like a number or a name in a spreadsheet cell, no longer get a period either. Say "period" if you want one. This works in apps that let Rhino read the text around the cursor; elsewhere nothing changes. - Dictating no longer replaces what you copied. Rhino pastes your words, then puts your previous clipboard back, and clipboard managers like Maccy, Paste and Raycast skip the dictation so it stays out of your history. To keep each dictation on the clipboard instead, turn on Settings > Output > Delivery > Copy to clipboard. If you turned it on yourself before, it stays on.

- AI cleanup is now on by default, and Settings → Output → Cleanup is down to three simple controls. After a few dictations, or the first time you dictate a list or an email, Home offers a one-click download of the cleanup model. - Double-tapping the dictation key no longer makes the bubble pop up, vanish and reappear. A quick double-tap now locks hands-free dictation on the same take. - Clicking Download on the cleanup model twice, or leaving Home mid-download, no longer starts a second 1 GB download or shows a false error after a good install. - Invite links now send friends straight to the free download.

- Transcripts of imported audio and video files can now include timestamps. Turn on Settings → Output → Imported files → Include timestamps, and each line starts with its time range in the recording. It's off by default, and dictation is unchanged.
